text: Biden says cancer will limit promotion of his new memoir. Joe Biden is trending after he said on Sunday that his cancer fight will limit how many interviews and events he can do to promote his memoir. The book, "Promise Me, America," is due out Nov. 17.. Former President Joe Biden announced the change in a post on social media. He wrote that some days are better than others and that the illness sometimes slows him down. He said he hopes readers will go to the book itself rather than rely on interviews. Biden revealed in May 2025, within months of leaving office, that he had prostate cancer. His office said at the time that the form was more aggressive but appeared to respond to hormone-based treatment. In August, his son Hunter Biden told the BBC that the cancer had spread to his bones and elsewhere. The memoir covers his four years as president, including the decisions he made and the challenges the country faced.. The memoir is scheduled for release on Nov. 17. Biden turns 84 on Nov. 20.

Sabonis is a Lithuanian-American player for the Kings and the Lithuanian national team. The rumors are not confirmed by the Kings, and no trade has been announced.. Rumors that the Kings may trade Sabonis have grown after a 0-4 start to the 2026-27 season. Teammate Zach LaVine's scoring and support for Sabonis have drawn attention to the situation.. A Yahoo Sports item dated Oct. 29, 2026 links to a commentary on a rumor that Sabonis wants the Kings to trade him. An SB Nation piece proposes trade packages built around Lauri Markkanen, Julius Randle and Naz Reid. That piece says the Jazz, Nets and Hornets are the teams that could benefit. These are proposals by a writer, not reported offers from those teams. On Oct. 28, 2026, Sabonis scored 20 points as the Kings lost 130-103 to San Antonio, and the loss left Sacramento at 0-4 to start the season. Sabonis is the son of Arvydas Sabonis, a Hall of Fame player, and he has been named to two All-NBA teams and three All-Star games. In the news: Teammate Zach LaVine scored 22 points in that loss and 28 in the season opener against the Clippers, and his support for Sabonis has drawn attention to the rumors during a slow start for the Kings.
